imageAlt: Teen golfer swings and misses the golf ball on the tee (air shot).

issues: Tee markers are red, which may not correspond to the most common tee used by teenage boys (usually white, yellow, or blue in many countries). However, this does not affect the accuracy for a general golf scene.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Use yellow, white, or blue tee markers to better match common teeing areas for teenage boys.

questions.title: If you swing and miss, does it count as a shot?
questions.question: You try to hit your ball from the tee, but you miss and don't touch it. Does that count as a shot?

choices.text: No, because you did not hit the ball.
Yes, it counts as a shot.
You must put your ball back on the tee and there's no penalty.
You can try again for free, but only once.

questions.explanation: If you swing at the ball and try to hit it but miss, it still counts as a shot. This is called an air shot.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: When you try to hit the ball but miss and do not touch it.
Another word for a shot. Every time you swing and mean to hit the ball, it counts as one stroke.

questions.teachingTip: Let children try some swings where they purposely miss the ball so they learn what an air shot feels like and understand that it counts.
likelyMisconceptions: Some might think missing the ball does not count, but it does if you tried to hit it.

questions.title: Does an air shot count as a stroke?
questions.question: If you swing at your ball on the tee and miss completely, does it count as a stroke?

choices.text: No, because you did not hit the ball.
Yes, it counts as a stroke.
You must re-tee your ball without penalty.
You can try again for free, but only once.

questions.explanation: Whenever you make a swing at the ball with the intention of hitting it, even if you miss (an air shot), it counts as a stroke.
